input.memo_markdown:
*All data in this report is synthetic.*

## Last week's moves
First run. Nothing to review.

## What's happening
- **LinkedIn:** $5,249 spent over 14 days with 0 conversions. Daily spend rose from ~$290 to ~$423. Before 10/18 it was already weak: CPA ~$185, ROAS 1.02. Self-reported LinkedIn share is 0% for the last 2 weeks.
- **Meta:** Spend is flat at ~$3.5k/wk. Weekly CPA went from ~$55-68 (Aug-Sep) to $130-156 (last 3 weeks), and ROAS from ~3.1 to ~1.3. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from 18% to 6%, so the drop is real and not only a tracking issue.
- **Direct:** Conversions rose from 1.8 to 7.6/day (4.2x) while paid spend moved 1.03x. Self-reported "AI assistant recommended you" plus "Asked ChatGPT" rose from ~7% to ~23%. The likely driver is AI-assistant referrals, which no paid channel caused.
- **Google Search:** Stable. CPA $17.13 vs $16.94 prior average, ROAS 11.2. The 9/12-9/18 spend spike is resolved.
- **Email:** Stable at $279/wk, CPA $18.59.

## Moves
- LinkedIn: $450 → $0/day. It has returned nothing for 14 days, and a pause is easy to reverse.
- Meta: $500 → $350/day. This is a partial cut because the models still credit it 14-22%.
- Google Search and Email: no change.

## Where the models disagree
- Google Search credit ranges from 39% (first-touch) to 69% (last-touch), so implied CPA is $19-33.
- Email credit ranges from 5% (last-touch) to 22% (first-touch), so implied CPA is $3.65-$16.74.
- Meta ($46-74 CPA) and LinkedIn ($93-197 CPA) are poor under every model, which is why those cuts don't depend on a single model.

## Test to run
- Google Search geo holdout: pause search in ~20% of matched regions for 3-4 weeks. Measure total conversions including direct.
- Email: hold out 10% of the list for 4 weeks.

## Confidence
Medium overall. LinkedIn is high confidence. Meta is medium confidence, because it is unclear whether the cause is creative fatigue or the shift toward AI discovery. I would reverse the Meta cut if the self-reported Instagram/Facebook share recovers, or if conversions fall further after the cut. I would revisit the Google Search budget after the holdout result.
